CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up for chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction prior to planned knee surgery.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Nicole Miller is a 76-year-old female presenting for follow-up of chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction. She was previously experiencing increasing dyspnea. Her furosemide was changed to torsemide 20 mg daily, and her lisinopril was increased to 10 mg daily in March. Patient reports weight loss of approximately 3 to 3.5 pounds since last visit in April. She states her urinary urgency has improved and she is breathing more easily. Patient experienced bilateral leg cramps a few days ago upon waking, which resolved after consuming pickle juice. She is scheduled for right knee replacement surgery on June 24th at East Metro and desires optimization of her cardiovascular status prior to surgery. She reports her heartburn resolved after taking Prilosec for two weeks in January and has had no recurrence since stopping that medication.

Patient denies current dyspnea. She experienced leg cramps recently that resolved. She denies current heartburn. She notes good urinary function. She confirms she remains on iron supplement and uses the bathroom without difficulty.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Weight down 3-3.5 pounds, breathing non-labored. Plan to repeat EKG today. Continue current medication regimen. Creatinine and labs appropriate.
